title: Convolution tensor descends to finite filtered homotopy localizations
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ be the homotopy category of uniformly finite decreasing filtered cochain complexes of $R$-modules and $W$ its graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. Let $\mathcal G_f(R)$ be its full subcategory of good complexes [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement]: their underlying, filtration-step and graded terms are flat, and their underlying, step and graded complexes are K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Put $\mathcal D_f(R)=\mathcal H_f(R)[W^{-1}]$, localization meaning formal inversion of $W$. Use the signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for the one-point ringed site with ring $R$, and the convolution filtration and canonical graded comparison of [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison].
Convolution tensor on good complexes descends to a bifunctor
$$\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]\times\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal G_f(R)[W^{-1}].$$
Transport along the good-replacement equivalence gives a bifunctor $\star:\mathcal D_f(R)\times\mathcal D_f(R)\to\mathcal D_f(R)$. Forgetting the filtration gives a functor $\omega:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$ and a natural isomorphism
$$\omega(U\star V)\cong\omega U\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\omega V,$$
where the right side is the ordinary derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$. For each $a$ the representative-level graded comparison descends to a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{gr}^a(U\star V)\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iU\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jV$$
in $D(R)$, for all morphisms of both localized variables. The sum is finite. On a pair of maps between good representatives these comparisons are the canonical maps induced by tensoring representatives and passing to their quotient classes; in particular the underlying morphism is the ordinary derived tensor of their underlying morphisms.

proof.text: The graded comparison supplies the actual convolution maps, their tensor formula, identities and composition, goodness, and preservation of graded quasi-isomorphisms. Using the filtered homotopy result, select chain-map representatives of homotopy-category maps and quotient the convolution tensor; independence follows from the quotient relation. This constructs a bifunctor on the good homotopy category with the required representative object and map formulas.

The private proof of Congruence gives the filtered homotopy relation its equivalence and composition laws. Grading followed by the ordinary derived quotient respects this relation. The characterization of graded quasi-isomorphisms in the two-out-of-three module shows that every chosen representative of a graded quasi-isomorphism has quasi-isomorphic graded maps. Thus the constructed bifunctor preserves denominators in both variables. Compose with the good localization and apply Localization.lift₂, with its inferred Lifting₂ witness.

Take the inclusion-compatible replacement equivalence from the replacement theorem. Precompose the localized bifunctor with its inverse in both variables and postcompose with its functor. The resulting star has τ = Iso.refl; naturality is the functor map-composition law.

For a complex-valued functor invariant under filtered homotopy after applying Q and sending graded quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, use Quotient.lift and then Localization.lift. Both the representative object pin and map pin are definitional. Apply this construction to forgetting, using the finite graded comparison, and separately to every grading, using the restricted and quotient homotopy construction.

Apply the separate comparison-descent theorem to precisely the functors, lifting witnesses, representative formulas and natural transport comparison just constructed. It supplies the underlying natural isomorphism and the graded isomorphisms on every finite support, with all canonical representative and support-enlargement equations. Combine these witnesses with the preceding constructions by the existential and conjunction constructors.
